title: Design the brand kit and reference library the model reads for every asset
scenario: Saltmarsh Soap orders about 60 images and clips a month from your studio. Several designers work on it. You design the brand kit and the reference library that every request reads. Use the exhibit. The notes are made up for this case; the vendor lines are copied from the docs.
exhibit:
BRIEF:
  Client: Saltmarsh Soap. Work: about 60 images and clips a month.
  Goal: one brand kit and one reference library that every request reads.

KIT (made up for this case):
  Card v3: "Look: soft studio photo, sea-glass green and cream.
           Rules: plain cream background. Voice: calm and short."
  Tuesday: a designer edited the card by hand to say "mint green" in 6 of the
           24 requests in one batch. The other 18 still say sea-glass green.

LIBRARY (made up for this case):
  Object set for the lavender bar: S-1, S-2, S-3. All three photos show the bar
           on the same wooden shelf. Every result from this set shows a
           wooden shelf.
  Search:  900 PNG, 400 JPEG, 60 WebP and 20 MP4 files, all under 4K x 4K.
           The File Search store was made with the default settings.

CAST (made up for this case):
  Gus the crab is a new character. Only a rough sketch exists. A side view
           will be needed.

RIGHTS (made up for this case):
  R-14:    Photo of freelancer Tomas holding a bar. Permission: "He said yes in
           the corridor." Nothing is on file. The art director wants R-14 as a
           character reference tomorrow.

VENDOR LINES (copied from the docs):
  OpenAI Skills:  "skill_reference.version accepts an integer or \"latest\"."
  Anthropic, advice for examples in a text prompt: "Diverse: Cover edge cases
           and vary enough that Claude doesn't pick up unintended patterns."
  Google File Search: "you must override the default text-only embedding model to
           use a multimodal model." "Supported formats are PNG, JPEG." "Audio and
           video formats are not currently supported."
  Google, 360 view: "include previously generated images in subsequent prompts to
           maintain consistency."
  Runway: "only use references of people you have permission to depict".

questions.prompt: Six of the 24 images show a different green. What is the best fix?

options.text: Keep the hand edits. Six mint images among 24 will not be noticed by the client, so leave it.
options.explanation: One campaign now has two greens. A client who knows the brand colours will see it, and the kit no longer matches the work.

options.text: Make one new kit version, update the card once, pin the number, and rerun all 24 requests.
options.explanation: Right. One kit version per batch, pinned by number, keeps the look the same. The OpenAI docs say a version can be a number or "latest".

options.text: Pin "latest" for the kit, so that every request picks up the newest wording by itself, always.
options.explanation: "latest" follows the newest upload. It would let the look change under a running batch.

options.text: Edit the other 18 requests by hand to say "mint green", so the whole batch matches again soon.
options.explanation: The batch would match, but the card would still say sea-glass green. Hand edits leave the kit and the work out of step.

questions.prompt: Every result from the lavender-bar set shows a wooden shelf. What is the best fix for the set?

options.text: Add two more photos of the bar on the shelf, so that the model sees the shelf is normal.
options.explanation: That makes the shelf even more common to every photo, so the model is more likely to copy it.

options.text: Fill the set up to the model's maximum, so the shelf becomes a smaller part of all references.
options.explanation: More images do not remove a shared detail. The shelf is still in the photos you keep, so the model still sees it.

options.text: Keep the set and add "no wooden shelf" to every prompt, so that the shelf is left out.
options.explanation: The cause is in the set. Fix what the three photos have in common instead of writing around it.

options.text: Swap two photos for ones on other surfaces, and keep the bar and its label the same in all three.
options.explanation: Right. This is our reading of Anthropic's advice that examples should be diverse: vary what you do not want copied.

questions.prompt: The team wants to search the library by look with Google File Search. What is the right plan?

options.text: Use a store made with gemini-embedding-2 for the 1,300 PNG and JPEG files, while WebP and MP4 stay out.
options.explanation: Right. The default is text-only. The Gemini API docs list PNG and JPEG as the image formats, and say audio and video are not supported.

options.text: Keep the store as it is and upload all 1,360 image files, because the model will read every format.
options.explanation: The default store is text-only, and the Gemini API docs list only PNG and JPEG. The WebP files are not listed.

options.text: Keep the store as it is and upload all 1,380 files, because File Search takes video as well.
options.explanation: The default store is text-only, and the Gemini API docs say audio and video formats are not currently supported.

options.text: Create a store with gemini-embedding-2, and upload all 1,380 files, including the 20 MP4 clips.
options.explanation: The embedding model is right, but the Gemini API docs say video is not currently supported. The clips would need another route.

questions.prompt: Gus needs a side view from his rough sketch. What is the best order of work?

options.text: Ask for the side view in words only and use it at once, since it will match the sketch well.
options.explanation: Google's method includes earlier images, and our rule is to check a view before using it. Words alone can drift.

options.text: Make a clean, neutral anchor, build the side view from it with earlier images, then check it.
options.explanation: Right. The Runway docs advise a clear, neutral reference for people, and we use it for any character. The Gemini API docs say to include previously generated images, and our rule adds the check.

options.text: Make all the views in one request, and approve the full set if only the last view looks right.
options.explanation: Each view should be checked against the anchor. A good last view says nothing about the others.

options.text: Use the first image the model makes as the anchor, and fix any problems later in the next images.
options.explanation: Everything else is built from the anchor, so a poor one spreads into all later views. Choose it with care.

questions.prompt: The art director wants R-14 as a character reference tomorrow. What do you do?

options.text: Use it. A spoken yes is permission, and the record can be filled in after the video is made.
options.explanation: The record is empty today. An asset with an empty field stays out of the sets until it is filled.

options.text: Keep it out of sets until his permission is written in the record. Ask what form is needed.
options.explanation: Right. The Runway docs say to use only references of people you have permission to depict. Which form counts is for the producer or a lawyer.

options.text: Use it, because the vendor, not the studio, is responsible for the rights to a likeness here.
options.explanation: The Runway docs say you are responsible for the rights to any likeness you submit.

options.text: Blur his face in the reference first, so that there is no likeness left to submit at all.
options.explanation: Runway wants a clear reference with the face visible. A blur does not remove the question of permission.
